mock_exam.weighting_note: 70% current module (14Q on M3, deliberately weighted toward levels 11-12 since those fall past the last checkpoint at level 10 and would otherwise go untested) / 30% previous phase-1 modules (3Q reviewing M1, 3Q reviewing M2).
mock_exam.structural_note: Module 3 has 12 levels, not a multiple of 5, so its 2 checkpoints (after L5, L10) leave levels 11-12 uncovered by any checkpoint — the same gap flagged for Module 14. Compensated here the same way: extra mock weight on those levels.

questions.prompt_en: Which spelling means 'two'?
questions.explanation_en: दौ is not a word — two marks above give the more open ौ, but this word needs the single-stroke ो.

questions.prompt_en: दुःख ('sorrow, pain') uses which mark?
questions.explanation_en: This is visarga ः, a light aspirated breath at the end of the syllable — distinct from both nasal marks.

questions.prompt_en: जगत् (a formal-register word for 'the world') ends with which mark, showing the final consonant has no vowel attached?
questions.explanation_en: The halant ् strips the inherent vowel from the final त, leaving a bare closing consonant sound.

questions.prompt_en: रास्ता ('road, way') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: स्त stacks स directly onto त with no vowel between.

questions.prompt_en: सम्पर्क ('contact') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: म्प stacks म onto प, both pronounced without a vowel between them.

questions.prompt_en: Which spelling means 'child'?
questions.explanation_en: The stack च्च is two plain ch sounds held together, not a single aspirated छ.

questions.prompt_en: सज्जन ('a gentleman, a good person') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: ज्ज stacks two ज sounds together.

questions.prompt_en: चप्पल ('sandal, slipper') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: प्प stacks two प sounds together, held slightly longer than a single प.

questions.prompt_en: दिल्ली ('Delhi') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: ल्ल stacks two ल sounds together.

questions.prompt_en: विश्वास ('trust, belief') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: श्व stacks श directly onto व.

questions.prompt_en: कष्ट ('trouble, hardship') uses which conjunct?
questions.explanation_en: ष्ट stacks ष onto ट.

questions.prompt_en: Which spelling is correct for 'lotus' (the flower)?
questions.explanation_en: The final अ is unwritten and silent — near-categorical word-final schwa deletion. Writing ा makes it real: कमला is a woman's name, not the flower.

questions.prompt_en: Which spelling is correct for 'pure, clean'?
questions.explanation_en: Not every conjunct keeps a final vowel. शुद्ध ends in a stop and behaves like any ordinary word ending — no extra ा belongs on it.

questions.prompt_en: Word-final schwa deletion (कमल = kamal, not kamala) is a firm, near-exceptionless rule. What about MEDIAL schwa deletion, as in समझ (samajh)?
options: Variable — depends on word structure and convention
questions.explanation_en: समझ keeps its medial schwa (samajh, not samjh), while other words drop theirs — नमस्ते drops the vowel after म. Medial deletion has to be learned word by word through audio and reading, not applied as a blanket rule.

questions.prompt_en: ईख ('sugarcane') opens with a long or short vowel?
questions.explanation_en: ईख carries the long ई, held roughly twice as long as इ.

questions.prompt_en: Which of these is NOT aspirated (no puff of breath)?
questions.explanation_en: कोना opens with plain क. The other three all open with an aspirated consonant.

questions.prompt_en: Which spelling means 'lentils'?
questions.explanation_en: The tongue touches the teeth for the dental द. Curling it back gives the retroflex ड and a different word, 'branch'.

questions.prompt_en: गाना ('song; to sing') begins with which letter?
questions.explanation_en: गाना opens with the plain, unaspirated ग.

questions.prompt_en: For व, do the lips close completely or stay apart?
questions.explanation_en: The lower lip only approaches the upper teeth for व. Closing the lips fully instead gives ब, a different letter.

questions.prompt_en: फ़ोन ('telephone') needs a dot on which letter to mark the f sound?
questions.explanation_en: Without the dot, फ is a p released with breath (ph). The dot marks the borrowed f sound specifically.
